title: Two added source panels preserve a gain test after any one panel is lost if planned worm responses qualify
abstract: We calculated added measurements that can test pair-specific response changes after separate source and target gains are allowed. We used the Randi worm response atlas and two adult Witvliet wiring maps. The selected base graph has 28 edges, 37 role vertices and no cycles, as a prior campaign study showed. Among 38 missing pairs with a detected normal response, two added source panels are necessary and sufficient to keep at least one independent gain constraint after all observations from any one source are removed. This is conditional on all planned additions yielding qualifying responses in both strains. Seven possible additions with direct wiring in either adult can supply two constraints, but cannot meet the source-loss rule. Four additions with direct wiring in both adults cannot supply any constraint within the fixed roles. We enumerated all source subsets and checked the optima with independent incidence-matrix ranks. This is a design result, not a biological strain effect, a trial budget or a power estimate. New code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and retrieval instructions permit exact reproduction. Named designs and source records are regenerated outside the baseline publication.

display.caption: Exact design capacity under four candidate rules and the best cycle count at each source-panel budget. Each new response must qualify in both strains. The cell roles and existing responses are fixed. The count is a gain-model constraint, not a recurrent anatomical loop or a statistical power estimate.
